text:
The Sharks arrive in Ottawa at game five of a six-game road trip, coming off a 4-3 overtime win at MTL on Tuesday in which they erased a two-goal deficit and Macklin Celebrini won it. They're 2-2-1 in their last five. The Senators beat FLA 5-1 last night and now play the second night of a back-to-back, without Thomas Chabot (upper body, estimated return Oct 27) and William Eklund (ankle, estimated return Jan 5). With Eklund out, Andre Burakovsky has moved beside Dylan Cozens, and Stephen Halliday and Drake Batherson are both playing more.

At five on five, SJS has taken 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, OTT 50%. The special-teams matchup to watch is the OTT power play, which creates 0.83 expected goals a game, against an SJS penalty kill that allows 0.96. OTT also takes 5.4 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Yaroslav Askarov (SJS) and Samuel Ersson (OTT) both finished last season below expected, at -19.4 and -17.75 goals saved above expected. This season Askarov sits at +0.48 and Ersson at -4.19.

Celebrini is 45% to score and 84% for a point, and Tim Stützle is 37% to score. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar picks are Halliday, a third-line forward whose shots have been dangerous lately, and Cozens, who is 51% for a point as his line creates chances against an SJS defence that gives up the third-most expected goals per 60.
